title: Example Assessment (synthetic)
subtitle: Three fictional technology groups, four assessment areas, every evidence state
disclaimer: SYNTHETIC EXAMPLE - fictional groups and fictional evidence. Not a University of Iowa finding.
_note: Every group, number and quotation in this file is invented to exercise the visual templates. Nothing here describes any real organization. Real inputs are UNKNOWN until collected.

cells.note: Written branching and review standard; two of five sampled fictional repositories follow a documented exception.
STRENGTH EXAMPLE. Fictional on-call rota, runbooks and postmortems agree with each other; eight of eight sampled incidents have a timeline and an owned follow-up action.

Dependency scanning runs on the main pipeline but not on the two fictional legacy pipelines. ZERO/NOT-RECORDED EXAMPLE: system records were searched and returned zero matching items (a measurement); no observed-artifact walkthrough was scheduled, so that kind is not recorded at all (an omission). The two must not render the same way.
Outside the agreed scope for this group in this fictional engagement. Not a rating, and not evidence of absence.

GAP EXAMPLE. No written delivery standard was produced for any of the fictional grant-funded projects, and three of four sampled projects had no review step at all. This is a finding about the group, not a statement about our evidence.

Maintenance windows are published and observed; recovery is evidenced for the shared cluster but not for the two fictional project-owned hosts. NOT-RECORDED EXAMPLE: no observed-artifact walkthrough was scheduled for any fictional RIS area, so that evidence kind is not recorded for this group. It is not zero.

CONTRADICTORY EXAMPLE. The written procedure and the change records give different answers. No single rating is supportable until the group explains whether these are undocumented exceptions or a procedure nobody follows. Both readings are kept.

conflict.says: two approvals are required for any production access change

conflict.source: Sampled change records, 12 fictional changes in the review window
conflict.says: seven of twelve record a single approval, with no documented exception

cells.note: Two fictional sources describe informal experimentation. Nothing supplied described inputs, ownership or review, so no rating is supportable.
Vendor release notes plus a local change record; local customization follows a written checklist.
Availability is reported by the fictional vendor; no local records were supplied, so the reported figures could not be corroborated.

Access review cadence is documented and the fictional sampled reviews were completed on schedule; two of six sampled records lacked a reviewer name. MEASURED-ZERO EXAMPLE: the observed-artifact walkthrough was carried out for every fictional IAM area and returned zero items. That is a measurement, not a missing entry.

NOT-APPLICABLE EXAMPLE. This fictional group runs a vendor-hosted core with no local model or data pipeline, so the AI-readiness questions do not apply to how it operates. This is a fact about the group's context, not a gap in our evidence.
